### Userland writer · Question

Event: `d63817e0bba46e2531ac3bf020cb8857` · 2026-09-26T08:01:42Z

> M2 (usable shell): 'interrupting and killing jobs (by budget destruction; no signals)'. Settled: no per-process kill; killing is destroying a budget, so the shell carves one budget per native stage (`Job.kill` destroys it). Undecided: what the interrupt key does. A runaway Elixir expression runs inside the session VM, which has no budget of its own to destroy. RECOMMENDATION: Ctrl+C at the line editor destroys the foreground job's budgets (every native stage of the pipeline) and, for Elixir work, kills the evaluating Erlang process with an untrappable exit (IEx starts a fresh evaluator; the session keeps its bindings as IEx does); Ctrl+G stays edlin's job-control menu. A job's budget is carved from the session's, so its end can never touch the session. Until answered the page lists this under Open.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `76bb897d6e48a69f380348afe6866005` · 2026-09-26T08:03:16Z

> Architect ruling, userland/shell.md, M2 (usable shell): the RECOMMENDATION is adopted, with four additions. Decided; nothing stays Open.
> 
> RULE:
> - Ctrl+C with a job in the foreground destroys every budget of that job's native stages. Each is carved from the session's budget, so its end never touches the session.
> - Elixir work is ended by killing the evaluating Erlang process with an untrappable exit (:kill). IEx starts a fresh evaluator.
> - Ctrl+C at an idle prompt clears the line. The BEAM break menu is never reachable. The session ends only by `exit` or Ctrl+D.
> - Ctrl+G stays edlin's job-control menu.
> 
> ADDITIONS:
> 1. The shell always sees the key. The session VM's I/O server reads /dev/cons continuously, not only while a line is being requested. A native stage never gets the raw console: its stdin is a pipe the session feeds. So no foreground program can swallow 0x03 and become uninterruptible. State this under What-it-cannot-do and test it with a native stage that reads stdin in a loop.
> 2. Bindings: do not promise that bindings survive. Say what IEx does, and back it with a test: an interrupt of `x = 1; loop()` leaves the session usable, and the page states whether `x` is still bound per that test's result. The guarantee is the session and its VM survive; its bindings are whatever IEx keeps.
> 3. Runaway memory, not only CPU. The evaluator runs with Erlang's max_heap_size process flag (kill: true), set to a fixed fraction of the session budget. A runaway allocation then kills the evaluator, as Ctrl+C would, instead of taking the whole session VM to its budget's page limit. Processes the expression spawned unlinked are not killed by Ctrl+C. The page says so and points to Job for background work.
> 4. Over SSH: sshd maps the SSH channel 'signal' request (INT) and 'break' request to the same interrupt event it would get from a 0x03 byte. It is a protocol message, not a Unix signal, and nothing inside Redoubt gains signals. Cross-link servers/sshd.md.
> 
> TESTS for M2 (usable shell):
> - interrupt a native `yes`-like stage: its budget is gone and the session is alive;
> - interrupt `loop()`;
> - a heap bomb is killed by max_heap_size;
> - a stdin-reading native stage cannot block Ctrl+C;
> - an SSH 'signal' INT interrupts.
